subject: Clarifying VPC packaging, platform fee amortization, and support tiers
messages:
From: Aarti Menon <aarti@hearthhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifying VPC packaging & platform fee amortization

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week — the latency numbers look promising for our inference workloads. Procurement asked me to get clarity on how Redwood is thinking about packaging for a private (VPC) deployment: specifically how the platform fee is structured across pilot → production, what you include in the implementation/migration retainer, and how support tiers map to response/oncall coverage.

Couple of concrete questions we need answered to move this internally:
- Can the platform fee be amortized between a 3-month pilot and a 12-month production commitment?
- If we don’t hit the committed throughput in month 1–3, do you offer credits or roll-forward adjustments?
- What’s included in the implementation retainer vs what’s billed as professional services?
- For support tiers, how many incident responses / SRE hours are included in each tier, and do you offer on-call rotations?

I attached the SOW template our legal team wants to align to (stub: Hearth_SOW_req.docx). We’d like a short written response we can circulate to finance/procurement. If you can include a worked example with numbers, that would be ideal.

Appreciate it —
Aarti
Procurement Manager, Hearth Health
procurement@hearthhealth.com
(attachment: Hearth_SOW_request_template.docx)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Aarti Menon <aarti@hearthhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying VPC packaging & platform fee amortization

Hi Aarti — thanks for the clear note and the SOW template. Below is a succinct proposal and a worked example so procurement has a concrete framing to circulate. I’ve kept the options intentionally simple so you can present them to Finance.

Summary of options (high level):
1) Pilot-first amortized model (recommended for proof-of-value)
   - 3-month pilot platform fee: $60,000 (covers runtime, base observability, prefix cache allocation)
   - Production annual platform fee (post-pilot): $180,000
   - Option to convert up to 50% of pilot platform fee into a migration retainer that is applied to PS hours in month 1–6 of production.
   - If committed throughput < 50% of forecast during pilot months, we provide a usage credit up to 30% of pilot fee, applied to future invoice within 12 months.

2) Accelerated commit (discounted annual anchor)
   - One-year platform fee: $150,000 (requires 12-month commit at defined throughput)
   - Implementation retainer included: $40,000 (covers initial integrations + one SRE onsite week)
   - Lower per-token runtime pricing compared with pay-as-you-go.

3) Minimal-risk trial (low pilot fee, higher implementation retainer)
   - Pilot platform fee: $25,000 + $75/hr PS retainer (billed monthly)
   - No automatic credits; designed if you want minimal upfront platform exposure.

Support tiers (short):
- Silver: 24x5 email + 8x5 oncall slack, 2 incident credits/month (standard SLA: 4 hour P1, 8 hour P2), monthly ops review.
- Gold: 24x7 oncall with dedicated escalation queue, 4 incident credits/month, quarterly architecture reviews, and a named SRE for onboarding during months 1–3.
- Platinum: Dedicated SRE hours (40 hours/mo), priority capacity reservations for bursts, and a quarterly health-check + remediation plan.

Worked example (Pilot-first amortized):
- Forecast: pilot expected to run 3 months at 100 rps, production expected 12 months at 250 rps.
- Pilot platform fee: $60k, elect to convert 50% ($30k) to migration retainer invoiced over first six months of prod (monthly $5k credit against PS invoices).
- If pilot usage < 50% of forecast in aggregate during months 1–3, Redwood issues a credit up to 30% × $60k = $18k applied to next year’s platform invoice or to PS balance.

Attachments: I’ve attached a draft SOW (Hearth_SOW_draft_v3.pdf), a pricing table (vpc-pricing-table-0309.xlsx), and a simple infra diagram (infra-arch.png). If this framing looks OK, I’ll route a short internal note to justify the credit & retainer path and get legal on the SOW edits.

If you want, we can set a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow afternoon to walk procurement through the examples.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
(attachment stubs: Hearth_SOW_draft_v3.pdf, vpc-pricing-table-0309.xlsx, infra-arch.png)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Hearth Health pricing ask (pilot amortization + credit ask)

Team — forwarding Aarti’s note and my reply. Quick context: Hearth is evaluating a VPC deployment; procurement wants explicit amortization and a credit mechanism if pilot utilization is low. I proposed a pilot-first amortized model with an option to convert pilot platform fee into migration retainer and a capped pilot-credit (30% of pilot fee) if utilization misses forecast.

Decision requested (I need sign-off/edits before I send the final SOW):
- Approve offering: pilot platform fee conversion up to 50% into migration retainer (applied to PS hours months 1–6)?
- Approve credit cap at 30% of pilot fee, redeemable against next year’s platform invoice OR PS balance?
- Do we require a minimum throughput floor (e.g., 40% of forecast) before credits are applicable? I suggested a 40% floor.
- Legal/Proc: Irene — any red flags with refundable credit language or how it’s shown in the SOW / invoice?

Impacts: revenue recognition will be split: pilot portion recognized on delivery; migration retainer recognized as deferred revenue and drawn vs PS. Credit accounting: credits applied as contra-revenue on next invoice; need Finance sign-off on how to present to Hearth.

I’m proposing to offer the pilot conversion + 30% cap for Hearth to lock pilot quickly. If approved, I’ll update the SOW and send to Aarti with a DocuSign template.

Thanks —
Soojin

[Quoted message from Aarti omitted for brevity — full text in thread above and attachments in Drive link]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 10:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Hearth Health pricing ask (pilot amortization + credit ask)

Soojin — thanks for the clear framing. I’m comfortable with the pilot conversion up to 50% into a migration retainer, provided we:

1) Move 70% of the retainer to a monthly invoiced credit (to improve cash flow visibility).
2) Limit credits to be applied only against Redwood invoices (platform or PS) within 12 months; no cash refunds.
3) Require the 40% throughput floor before credits trigger.

Ben — can you set a hard cap on the total credit exposure we’re willing to accept per account for this tier? I’d suggest $25k absolute cap beyond which we escalate to Head of Sales. Also make sure SRE hours in Gold tier are tracked in PagerDuty and tied to invoiceable overruns.

Irene — happy to fold SOC2 artifact checklist into the SOW as an appendix so procurement has compliance items upfront.

I approve with the above guardrails.

Marissa
Director, Commercial

(attachment: pricing-commentary-0309.txt)

From: Aarti Menon <aarti@hearthhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Hearth Health Procurement <procurement@hearthhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Mar 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying VPC packaging & platform fee amortization

Soojin — thanks for the detailed options and worked example. Hearth is comfortable moving forward with the Pilot-first amortized model you proposed, subject to the following (procurement sign-off):

- Pilot fee $60k with option to convert up to $30k into migration retainer (monthly credit drawn over first 6 months).
- Credit trigger: aggregate pilot usage < 50% of forecast → credit up to 18k (you listed 30% cap, we accept if limited to Redwood invoices only).
- Include SOC2 checklist and our standard SOW appendix (I attached a short redline).

Please send the updated SOW with the credit/retainer language and a DocuSign link. We aim to finish procurement review by Mar 28 so engineering can schedule the pilot kickoff in early April.

I’ll loop in legal if there are unusual contract terms.

Thanks —
Aarti
Procurement Manager, Hearth Health
(Confirms receipt of attachments: Hearth_SOW_draft_v3.pdf, vpc-pricing-table-0309.xlsx)
